The Education

Why OT Billing Has Three Distinct Revenue Challenges Simultaneously

Occupational therapy billing covers therapeutic activities, ADL training, hand therapy, custom orthotic fabrication, cognitive rehabilitation, and sensory integration. Medicare OT billing is governed by annual therapy thresholds claims above the threshold require the KX modifier indicating medical necessity. Without the KX modifier, claims are auto-denied.

Custom orthotic fabrication (L-codes) is the most systematically missed revenue in hand therapy. Most practices fabricate custom splints daily without billing the L-code $150 to $480 per device in additional revenue permanently lost. PMEx implements L-code billing from the first custom device fabricated.

Pediatric OT diagnosis coding requires specific ICD-10 codes linking to documented functional limitations. Vague developmental delay coding results in systematic medical necessity denials. PMEx implements diagnosis-specific coding that supports medical necessity for autism, sensory processing disorder, and developmental coordination disorder.

The KX Modifier and Medicare Therapy Threshold

The KX Modifier + L-Code Custom Orthotic Revenue Gap

When a Medicare OT patient's annual therapy utilization reaches the targeted review threshold, every subsequent claim must carry the KX modifier indicating medical necessity documentation exists and supports continued care. Without the KX modifier, the claim is automatically denied. The documentation must be specific and complete: general statements like "patient continues to benefit" do not meet targeted review standards.

The L-code orthotic billing gap runs parallel to the KX modifier issue in hand therapy. Custom static and dynamic splints are separately billable with HCPCS L-codes L3900 for dynamic splints, L3908 for wrist extension orthosis, L3000+ for custom molded foot orthotics. Most hand therapy practices fabricate these devices daily and bill only the therapeutic session, leaving the device revenue entirely uncaptured.
